title: Mapping the sensory-neuron zoo
objective: Explain how single-cell atlases turned sensory neurons into defined molecular subtypes.

steps.title: From 'small, medium, large' to a parts list
steps.body: Sensory neurons were once sorted mostly by size and conduction. **[[single-cell RNA sequencing]]** changed that: profiling thousands of [[DRG]] neurons one at a time gave a molecular parts list — defined subtypes, each with marker genes you can target.

steps.prompt: What did single-cell atlases add beyond classic size/conduction classes?
options: Molecular subtypes with marker genes you can genetically target
A direct read-out of what each subtype actually senses in vivo
Exact firing thresholds measured for each neuron that was profiled
A way to avoid ever having to use RNAscope validation
steps.explanation: Atlases define subtypes by gene expression, handing you markers to build Cre lines around — the bridge from description to manipulation. They don't change conduction, and they reveal diversity, not uniformity.

variants.setup: scRNA-seq profiles thousands of individual DRG neurons.
options: A direct read-out of what each subtype senses
Firing thresholds for each neuron profiled
variants.reveal: Atlases yield targetable molecular subtypes — the handle for genetic access.

steps.prompt: A molecular atlas gives you a candidate subtype. What's still needed to study its function?
options: Genetic access (a marker-based Cre line and tools) to reach those cells
Deeper sequencing of the same neurons to confirm the marker gene
An antibody stain showing the marker protein in fixed tissue
A larger sample of dissected tissue to sequence in bulk
steps.explanation: An atlas is a description. Testing function needs a way to label and manipulate the subtype in vivo — the C-track pipeline — not just more imaging or tissue.

variants.setup: You have a subtype and its marker from an atlas.
variants.prompt: What's required to test what it does?
options: Deeper sequencing of the same cells
An antibody stain in fixed tissue
variants.reveal: You need a Cre line and tools to manipulate the subtype — the atlas only names it.
